title: Dark-mode and accessibility pass for onboarding assets and quickstart visuals
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Perform a focused accessibility and dark-mode review for all onboarding / quickstart UX assets (illustrations, iconography, screenshots, and docs visuals) used in the public quickstart flow and internal 'first-run' product tour. Goal: meet WCAG AA contrast for text and interactive elements, ensure imagery and icons are readable in dark contexts, provide alternate assets and implementation guidance so engineering can swap assets without visual regressions.
acceptance_criteria: All onboarding screenshots (desktop+mobile) have dark-mode variants with consistent visual hierarchy and file names following the naming convention.
Primary CTA buttons meet WCAG AA contrast ratio (>=4.5:1) against background in both light and dark themes.
Iconography has stroke/fill variants for dark mode; decorative illustrations include high-contrast outline fallback where needed.
Figma library updated with semantic color tokens and exported SVG/PNG asset sets; link to board provided.
QA checklist passes automated contrast tests (axe/lighthouse) and manual spot checks on macOS/iOS/Windows with system dark-mode enabled.
Engineering acceptance: simple theme token mapping (token names unchanged) allows automatic swapping of assets via existing console theme switch.
Documentation updated with alt text guidance and a short note on 'reduce motion' handling for animated intro assets.
tasks: Audit current onboarding assets: collect list of screenshots, illustrations, and icons used in quickstart pages and in-app tour.
Create high-contrast variants for three decorative illustrations used on the welcome and API key screens.
Design iconography stroke-width and fill rules for dark mode (outline vs. filled decisions), produce export-ready SVGs.
Retake product screenshots in dark-mode with updated copy overlay styles (shadow/blur adjustments) and add to Drive folder.
Update Figma tokens: define semantic tokens for surface, text, muted, accent, and interactive states; add dark-mode values.
Write implementation notes for engineering (token mapping, aria-hidden for decorative SVGs, recommended CSS for image rendering).
Run automated contrast reports and iterate until all primary flows pass AA; capture results as artifacts.
design_decisions: Use semantic color tokens (eg. --onboarding-surface, --onboarding-text-high, --onboarding-accent) so engineering can swap themes without changing asset names.
Prefer slightly heavier icon strokes in dark mode (+0.5px visual weight) rather than increasing icon size to preserve layout consistency.
Provide two variants for decorative illustrations: full-color for light mode, simplified high-contrast outline for dark mode to avoid color mud.
Keep CTA primary color the same token across themes but adjust luminance for contrast; accessibility takes priority over exact brand hue in dark mode.
tradeoffs: Increasing stroke weight and contrast reduces delicate visual feel in dark mode; accepted to meet legibility requirements.
Providing separate illustration variants increases maintenance overhead (two asset sets) but ensures clear readability for users with low vision.
Some screenshots require slight re-layout in dark mode (e.g., dialogs need less transparency); will coordinate with frontend to avoid breaking screenshots used in docs.

qa_checklist: Automated contrast report uploaded to ticket attachments
Manual spot-checks on macOS (Safari+Chrome), Windows (Edge+Chrome), iOS 16+, Android 12+
Verify alt text for all illustrative images in docs and mark decorative SVGs with aria-hidden
Confirm Figma tokens match tokens used in frontend PR
Verify no layout breakage in docs when swapping screenshot variants
notes_for_engineering: Token mapping PR includes example CSS variables and a small helper to swap assets based on theme; prefer using token-only switches to keep markup unchanged.
Decorative SVGs should include role=img and aria-hidden=true when decorative, and an accessible SVG with <title> only when content-relevant.
For animated intro assets, respect 'prefers-reduced-motion' and provide static fallback PNGs in the same naming convention.
When exporting PNGs, use 2x retina exports for mobile screenshots and optimize with lossless compression to avoid artifacts in dark backgrounds.
